Synopsis:
Canada's Q2 2026 GDP grew at an annualized 3.3% — the strongest since 2023 — beating the Bank of Canada's 2.5% forecast, and avoiding a technical recession after Q1 was revised up to +0.3%. Growth was driven by a 3.6% surge in exports (3-year high), recovering domestic demand (+1.0%), rising consumer spending (+0.8%), and the first business investment expansion in 18 months (+2.3%). However, a new U.S. 50% tariff on $20B of Canadian exports — imposed by Trump this week — injects fresh uncertainty. Money markets price no BoC rate change next week. July GDP is tracking flat.
